# Fairstay Change of Ownership (`fairstay-change-of-ownership`)

Change of ownership (CHOW) tracker for nursing homes: every step for Medicare, Medicaid, the state license, payers, banking, payroll, insurance and vendors against the closing date, with late steps, blocked steps, steps due soon and standard steps missing from your list. Agency contact details are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Change of Ownership never files anything with CMS, a Medicare contractor or a state.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Change of ownership and licensing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-change-of-ownership demo
npx -y fairstay-change-of-ownership mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional change of ownership at Cedar Hollow, closing 1 July 2026, checked on 1 April 2026. Planted:

- The state license application was due 25 March and is not filed (late).
- Medicaid CHOW enrollment waits on the Medicare CMS-855A, which is not filed (blocked). The 855A itself waited on the new EIN and NPI, which are done, so it is only due soon (2 April).
- Managed care credentialing (2 April) and vendor contracts (10 April) are due soon.
- The list has no step for the Medicare provider agreement decision, CLIA, CMS systems access (PBJ, iQIES) or the seller's terminating cost report.

Agency emails are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells `close_date` as `closing`, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `chow_check` | Check the CHOW checklist against the closing date and the standard steps. | runs |
| `chow_write_report` | Write chow.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and chow.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/chow). | runs |
| `chow_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `chow_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `chow_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `chow_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `agency_filing_submit` | Fairstay Change of Ownership never files anything with CMS, a Medicare contractor or a state. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `chow_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `steps` (required) | CHOW checklist under --root: step, area, owner, due date or days before close, done date, blocked by, agency contact |
| `deal` (required) | Deal JSON: close_date, warn_days |
| `as_of` | Status date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-change-of-ownership inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### CHOW checklist (`steps`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `step` (required) | text | Step, Task, Item, Description |
| `area` | text | Area, Category, Workstream, Agency |
| `owner` | text | Owner, Responsible, Assigned To |
| `due` | date | Due, Due Date, Deadline |
| `days_before_close` | number | Days Before Close, Lead Days, Days Before Closing |
| `done_on` | date | Done, Done On, Completed, Filed On |
| `blocked_by` | text | Blocked By, Depends On, Waiting On |
| `contact_email` | text (masked) | Contact Email, Agency Contact, Email |

## Settings file (`chow_deal`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `close_date` (required) | Planned closing (effective) date |
| `warn_days` | Flag steps due within this many days (default 14) |

## Memory

`chow_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `chow_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `chow_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-change-of-ownership": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-change-of-ownership",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-change-of-ownership -- npx -y fairstay-change-of-ownership mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-change-of-ownership tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-change-of-ownership sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-change-of-ownership inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-change-of-ownership call chow_check '{"steps":"<steps>","deal":"<deal>"}'
fairstay-change-of-ownership eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-change-of-ownership demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
